title: Concurrent Rollout Pacebook and Team Handoff Grid
body:
Purpose:
This note defines a lightweight 'pacebook' for running concurrent rollouts across multiple cohorts, plus a concise team handoff grid. Goal: reduce ambiguity during overlapping launches and make day-of decisions predictable, with low cognitive overhead for on-call and engineers running the rollout.

Scope:
- Applies to all infra+runtime releases that will be rolled out by cohort (region, customer tier, or traffic slice).
- Not intended for emergency hotfixes (use emergency runbook) or full datacenter migrations.

Key dates (proposal):
- Nov 15 09:00 PT — Start internal dry run (staging traffic mirroring)
- Nov 17 02:00 PT — Canary cohort A (1% global traffic)
- Nov 18 10:00 PT — Cohort B (5% traffic)
- Nov 19 14:00 PT — Cohort C (25% traffic)
- Nov 20 18:00 PT — Ramp to 100% per dependent teams signoff

Definitions — what a pacebook is here:
- Pacebook: a minimal, timeboxed cadence guide: when to execute checks, expect telemetry baselines, escalate, and perform handoffs. Think of it as the heartbeat of the rollout (check, wait, evaluate, move).
- Cohort: any logical traffic slice (can be by region, model variant, or customer segment).
- Quiet window: pre-deploy period where nonblocking changes are avoided and sampling/telemetry baselines are captured.

Concurrent rollout constraints (rules):
1) No more than two cohort ramps in parallel that change model routing.
2) Only one cohort may perform model-architecture changes per 24h window.
3) If two teams are pushing related surface-area changes (API schema, token billing), schedule serially or merge into a single controlled rollout.
4) Region-localized cohorts can run independently if routing/traffic isolation is guaranteed.

Preflight checklist (to run 24–2 hours before cohort A):
- [ ] Confirm smoke tests green on staging for sequence lengths up to 2048 tokens.
- [ ] Verify autoscale policies: target p95 latency margins configured + safety cushion (20%).
- [ ] KV cache priming test for representative prompts.
- [ ] Canary synthetic traffic script created and validated (JMeter/locust snippet).
- [ ] Observability: dashboards pinned, alert rules enabled, sampling rate set to 10% for traces.
- [ ] Pager duty coverage confirmed for 0–72h post cohort.
- [ ] Key stakeholders notified (product, infra, SRE, security).
- [ ] Rollback artifact built and smoke-verified.

Day-of pacebook (hourly heartbeat template):
- T0: deploy to canary k8s pool; note commit and image hash.
- T+5m: quick sanity smoke (3 golden requests) — confirm responses and token counts.
- T+30m: baseline telemetry capture (p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, CPU/GPU util).
- T+60m: extend to cohort target; run 30m sampling of customer-like traffic.
- T+120m: team review; decide to advance or rollback. If advancing, follow same cadence for next cohort.

Handoff grid (who does what) — compact, one-line responsibilities per role:
- Release owner: Maya Patel — overall go/no-go authority, final signoff on cohort transitions.
- Infra lead: Jonas Rivera — scaling knobs, pool capacity and infra fixes.
- Runtime/serving lead: Priya Singh — model variant mapping, KV caching config changes.
- Observability & SRE: Ethan Moore — dashboards, alerts, triage coordination.
- Product/QA: Lina Gomez — feature gating verification, customer-impact checks.
- Security & Compliance contact: Omar Alvi — any auth/KMS anomalies.
- On-call eng: rotation per PD schedule — immediate incident response and rollback trigger.

Handoff rules and artifacts:
- Every transition between cohorts requires: one-line summary in #release-runner Slack, update to the rollout spreadsheet row, and the commit/image hash posted to the release thread.
- If the release owner is unavailable, infra lead assumes temporary ownership for decision windows < 2h; otherwise escalate to engineering manager.

Rollback pathways (decision ladder):
- Soft rollback: scale down new variant weights to 0 over 5 minutes and reintroduce previous variant weights (fast path for routing misbehavior).
- Full rollback: revert deployment to previous image and trigger orchestrated cache eviction (if necessary) — estimated 10–15 mins to stabilize but dependent on KV consistency.
- Emergency abort: use traffic cut policy to route traffic to Dedicated fallback tier; this must be preapproved and tested.

Telemetry guardrails and SLIs to watch (live):
- Request error rate (5xx or internal error) — alarm threshold: sustained > 0.5% for 5m.
- Latency p95 (generation + RPC) — alarm if > baseline + 30% sustained 10m.
- Token cost per request spike — watch token count anomalies vs expected prompt sizes.
- GPU memory OOM rate, thrash events, and kernel fallbacks.
- Quality regression signal: automated eval endpoint failure rate + regression alerts from sample prompt set.

Minimal public-facing release notes draft (to be cleaned by product):
- Short: "Improved serving runtime: model routing stability and autoscaling improvements for lower latency at high concurrency. Minor API smoothing for multi-segment prompts."
- Details: "This rollout updates the serving runtime to better manage KV cache priming and introduces a routing optimization that reduces cold-start latency for longer sequences. Expect improved tail latency for high-concurrency workloads. No customer-facing API changes; SDKs unaffected."
- Known issues: "In rare sequences with >3000 tokens and legacy quantized variants, token counting may misreport leading to slightly elevated token billing metrics — monitoring in place, fix targeted in next patch."

Open questions and TBDs:
- Do we permit parallel cohort ramps if cohorts target disjoint model families? (proposal: yes with tag-based isolation)
- Confirm final quiet window length with product telemetry team — current draft 90 minutes before deploy.
- Validate rollback times in a full-stress test for region EU-WEST-2.

Action items (owners):
- Jonas: run staging priming run and post results (by Nov 10).
- Priya: prepare KV priming checklist and snippet (by Nov 12).
- Ethan: create a condensed watchboard with top 6 signals and alert runbook (by Nov 13).
- Lina: prepare the customer note draft for legal review (by Nov 16).

Notes to self / runbook hygiene:
- Keep the pacebook intentionally short — long prose is a liability during incident windows.
- Favor one-line decisions in Slack + link to rollout spreadsheet; follow with a single confluence link for deeper context.

Revision history:
- 2026-11-02 Maya: initial sketch and pacing rules.
- 2026-11-09 Jonas: added preflight infra checklist items.
- 2026-11-14 Priya: refined KV and rollback steps; updated key dates.

If anything in this document conflicts with the emergency runbook, emergency runbook overrides.

-- end of draft --
